claims.text: Refining and homogenizing the nanoscale oxide dispersoid distribution will reduce high-temperature plastic strain relative to a conventional oxide dispersion.
Refining and homogenizing the nanoscale oxide dispersoid distribution will enhance toughness relative to a conventional oxide dispersion.
Controlled heat treatment or alloying adjustments can create a finer and more uniform distribution of nanoscale oxide particles.
A refined and uniform oxide distribution enhances dislocation pinning.
A refined and uniform oxide distribution enhances grain-boundary pinning.
Enhanced oxide-dispersoid pinning limits dislocation mobility.
Enhanced oxide-dispersoid pinning retards dynamic recovery and recrystallization.
Limited dislocation mobility and delayed dynamic recovery or recrystallization reduce plastic-strain accumulation.
Limited dislocation mobility and delayed dynamic recovery or recrystallization improve toughness.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate between approximately 800°C and 1200°C.
Temperatures of 800–1200°C are representative of high-temperature conditions relevant to fusion plasma-facing components.
Concurrent radiation damage or other thermal-degradation processes may interfere with the proposed oxide-dispersion mechanism.
Preliminary evidence supports a role for refined oxide dispersoids in enhancing mechanical properties.
